subject: Go-live guardrails and acceptance gates for HelioCorp deployment
messages:
From: Samantha Park <samantha@avasolutions.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: mike.hung@heliocorp.com
Date: 2025-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: go-live plan & acceptance criteria for HelioCorp deployment

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HelioCorp is keen to lock down an implementation timeline so we can coordinate infra and procurement. Attached is our high-level launch spreadsheet (HelioCorp wants a tightly scoped Phase 1). Can you share a mutual action plan with milestone owners, dates, and explicit acceptance gates (what does "go/no-go" look like)?

Key asks from our side:
- Clear milestone owners for Redwood, HelioCorp Eng, and HelioCorp Ops
- Acceptance tests (latency/throughput targets, smoke tests, privacy controls)
- Planned dry-run date(s) and rollback window
- Any items that require customer procurement lead time (network peering, certs)

We'd like to target a production go-live in the week of Aug 11 if that's feasible.

Can you get a draft MAP by end of day tomorrow?

Thanks,
Samantha Park
Director, Platform Operations
Ava Solutions (on behalf of HelioCorp)
Attachment: HelioCorp_MAP_request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Samantha Park <samantha@avasolutions.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mike.hung@heliocorp.com
Date: 2025-07-20T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: go-live plan & acceptance criteria for HelioCorp deployment

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks. Draft attached: HLC_MAP_v0.1.xlsx. Below is a concise mutual action plan and proposed acceptance gates for Phase 1 (we kept the scope narrow to meet your Aug 11 target):

High-level milestones (owner — target date):
- Contract & SOW signed (HelioCorp Legal / HelioCorp) — Jul 22
- Provision Dedicated Capacity & VPC peering (Redwood Infra / Redwood) — Jul 28
- Integration sprint 1: Auth & API keys (HelioCorp Eng / HelioCorp) — Jul 30
- Integration sprint 2: Data flows & KV caching validation (Redwood Eng / Redwood) — Aug 04
- Dry run (technical): smoke + perf test (joint) — Aug 08
- Final acceptance window (customer sign-off) — Aug 11

Acceptance gates (go/no-go):
1) Networking & access: VPC peering established, egress rules validated, certs exchanged.
2) Functional: End-to-end generation calls (sample prompts) return valid responses for 95% of test prompts used in eval set.
3) Performance: 99th percentile latency under 350ms for representative 512-token requests during dry run (burst traffic simulated).
4) Reliability: No more than 2% error rate during a 30-minute stability window at expected baseline throughput.
5) Security/compliance: Audit logs enabled, key rotation process confirmed, and retention policy agreed.

Immediate open items for HelioCorp:
- Confirm procurement lead time for peering (network ticket) and provide contact for cert exchange.
- Provide the canonical eval prompt set and expected baseline QPS.

Attachments: HLC_MAP_v0.1.xlsx (draft MAP) — I added owners and suggested dates. Link to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bHLC-Helio-Launch

Marissa and Karthik, tagging you for runbook and acceptance-test owners: can you confirm the dry-run playbook and smoke-test checklist by tomorrow EOD?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: HLC_MAP_v0.1.xlsx (draft spreadsheet)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Samantha Park <samantha@avasolutions.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mike.hung@heliocorp.com
Date: 2025-07-20T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: go-live plan & acceptance criteria for HelioCorp deployment

Samantha / Markus —

Quick implementation runbook highlights and the acceptance-test checklist (attached PDF). Key points we will own as CS/Implementation:

Implementation runbook (Redwood responsibilities):
- Pre-provisioning validation: account config, tokens, and RBAC — target Jul 27
- Autoscaling policy baseline configured for Phase 1 (cost/latency trade-offs) — Jul 29
- Canary model variant configured + fallback route for capacity constraints — Aug 05
- Monitoring & alerting: per-route latency dashboards, token breakdown, and error traces — Aug 06

Acceptance-test checklist (joint):
- Smoke test: 20 canonical prompts, functional correctness spot-check (HelioCorp QA leads)
- Perf test: 15-minute ramp to baseline QPS + 5-minute burst at 2x QPS; measure p50/p95/p99
- Failover: simulated node failure while maintaining <10% increase in latency for steady-state traffic
- Security: verify KMS integration for key material and confirm audit log visibility in console

Dry-run logistics: we propose Aug 08 at 10:00 AM PT for the full technical dry run. That gives us three days to remediate before the Aug 11 acceptance window. Please confirm whether HelioCorp can staff: Eng lead, QA lead, and Network/Infra contact.

Attachments: implementation-runbook.pdf (checklist + step-by-step), runbook link in shared folder.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
Attachment: implementation-runbook.pdf (runbook + checklist)

From: Mike Hung <mike.hung@heliocorp.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, Samantha Park <samantha@avasolutions.com>
Date: 2025-07-21T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: go-live plan & acceptance criteria for HelioCorp deployment

Thanks — this looks actionable. A couple quick clarifications from HelioCorp Ops before we lock dates: 

1) Dry run staffing: Confirmed. I'll be present with our Eng lead (Priya Rao) and QA (Dev Patel).
2) Data retention: we need a 90-day logs retention window and the ability to export audit logs to our S3 bucket. Is there an automated export we should enable on Redwood Dedicated?
3) Private deployment question: for regulatory reasons, is there any additional lead time for an on-prem/private control-plane install (we might need it later for Phase 2)? If so, call it out in the MAP so we can set procurement timelines.

We can do the dry run Aug 08 10:00 AM PT as proposed. One ask: can Redwood run a short KV cache warm-up prior to the dry run so the perf numbers reflect warm-cache performance?

If you can confirm the export path for audit logs and add a Phase 2 note re: private control plane lead time, we'll accept the draft and move to SOW signature next week.

Mike Hung
Director, Platform Engineering
HelioCorp
